H&P – Super Detailed Clinical Note  

Consult Summary:  
40-year-old postpartum woman (4 weeks after C-section) with sudden-onset shortness of breath and tachycardia at rest; high clinical concern for pulmonary embolism → advised urgent hospital evaluation.

History:  
• Presenting complaint – “short of breath” for ≈1 hour while sitting watching TV.  
• Chronology – abrupt onset, no previous similar episodes.  
• Associated symptoms  
  – Dry cough began yesterday.  
  – Palpitations/awareness of rapid heartbeat.  
  – Soreness in chest on deep inspiration; C-section scar also tender.  
  – Denies frank chest pain at rest; no sputum, hemoptysis, fever, leg pain/swelling reported.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors – stress appears to worsen awareness of heartbeat; no clear relievers.  
• ROS – other systems not discussed in transcript.

Past Medical History:  
• Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; recovery otherwise unremarkable.  
• No chronic illnesses mentioned.

Medications:  
• Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); taken regularly after surgery, last dose about 1 week ago.  
• No current anticoagulants or other meds noted.

Allergies:  
• Ibuprofen – reaction not specified.

Social History:  
• Lives at home with 4-week-old baby; partner at work during call.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use – not discussed.  
• Able to self-transport to hospital; no other support details provided.

Family History:  
• Mother with history of leg clots (DVT).  
• No other family illnesses mentioned.

Physical Examination:  
• Vitals – patient counted 30 radial pulses over clinician-timed interval (interpreted by clinician as “slightly fast,” ≈120 bpm → tachycardia).  
• No additional vital signs or systemic examination recorded.

Investigations:  
• None performed during virtual visit.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath, suspected pulmonary embolism (highest concern).  
  • Rationale: sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, 4-week postpartum status post-C-section, family history of DVT, pleuritic-type discomfort.  
  • Plan:  
    – Advised immediate hospital evaluation today.  
    – Discussed transport options; patient elected to self-present rather than ambulance.  
    – Take essentials for baby; travel promptly.  
    – Hold further codeine until assessed.  
    – Hospital to perform appropriate work-up (e.g., vitals, ECG, D-dimer, CTPA, anticoagulation) – per ED protocol (implied by clinician recommendation).

Issue 2: Post-Cesarean postoperative care.  
  • No acute complications apart from above; scar tender but expected.  
  • Plan: routine postpartum follow-up continues; no new meds started; avoid NSAIDs due to allergy.

Issue 3: New dry cough.  
  • Etiology uncertain (infection vs irritation vs PE).  
  • Plan: will be assessed concurrently in ED; no outpatient treatment initiated.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):  
1. Pulmonary embolism – High likelihood: classic risk factors (recent surgery, postpartum, family history) and presentation (sudden SOB, tachycardia, pleuritic discomfort).  
2. Acute respiratory infection (viral/bacterial) – Moderate likelihood: preceding cough, but absence of fever/sputum and abrupt dyspnea onset argues against.  
3. Anxiety/panic attack – Moderate but less likely: patient feels stressed with palpitations, yet objective risk factors and pleuritic discomfort favor organic cause.

Quality checks (document_quality):  
• Missing but expected: complete vitals (BP, RR, SpO₂, temp), medication reconciliation (prenatal vitamins, others), detailed allergy reaction, obstetric history (gravida/para), smoking/alcohol status.  
• Transcript/DDx conflicts: DOB stated 20 Apr 1980 by patient vs 1983 echoed by clinician – conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear; no major audio gaps, but limited ROS and physical data inherent to video visit.
